newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: DB on track to at least maintain EBIT.
newsitem.headline: DB on track to at least maintain EBIT.

text.p: New Zealand brewer DB Group Ltd said on Wednesday its 1997 results to date indicated it was on track to maintain or even improve EBIT (earnings before interest and tax) performance despite a declining market.
Chairman David Sadler told the annual meeting the group had achieved a strong financial performance and met the board's expectations for the year ended September 30, 1996.
Sadler also addressed shareholders on the proposal to reduce DB Group's capital by returning approximately NZ$180 million to shareholders pro rata.

"The group will continue its strategy of sticking closely to its core business of producing and marketing beer, wines and spirits in New Zealand and will not be investing in any liquor businesses overseas or other industries in New Zealand or anywhere else," he said.
"Accordingly, after the capital reduction the group will be adequately capitalised to carry out its business objectives in the New Zealand liquor industry."
Managing Director Erik Korthals Altes confirmed the company's commitment to long term brand building across its portfolios in beer, wine and spirits.
"The expected ongoing improvement in discretionary income will increase the number of discerning consumers and continue to support "trade up" trends.
"We are ready to cash in on these trends with strong brands such as Heineken, DB Draught, Export Gold, Stoneleigh Wines, Jim Beam and Absolut Vodka."
DB is 59.8 percent owned by Asia Pacific Breweries Ltd, a venture between Heineken NV and Fraser and Neave Ltd .
